items.name: FileZilla
items.blurb: Transfer files by FTP and SFTP.

style.label: Photoshop Layout
style.blurb: Photoshop Layout arranges GIMP's tools, panels and shortcuts like Photoshop's (PhotoGIMP by Diolinux, GPL-3.0). Quit GIMP before switching; Standard Layout puts your own settings back.

style.label: Illustrator Layout
style.blurb: Illustrator Layout switches Inkscape to Illustrator-style keyboard shortcuts: V to select, A for nodes, P for the pen, T for text, M and L for shapes.

items.name: Shotwell
items.blurb: Organize and touch up your photographs.

items.name: VLC
items.blurb: Play almost any video or sound file.

items.name: Mines
items.blurb: Find the mines without digging one up.

items.name: Quadrapassel
items.blurb: Falling blocks; don't let them reach the top.

items.name: Archive Utility
items.blurb: Open and make Zip and other archives.

items.name: Hue Lights
items.blurb: Philips Hue lights in The Collar: turn the rooms you choose on and off, set their brightness and pick their scenes. Press the bridge's link button, then choose Connect from the Hue module.

items.name: Turntable
items.blurb: Listen to a USB turntable through your speakers or TV, switched on and off from The Collar. Plug the turntable in, then choose On from the Turntable module. Left on, it plays again whenever the turntable is plugged in.

items.name: Phone
items.blurb: KDE Connect and Syncthing for your phone: notifications, file sharing, clipboard and photo sync. Installs KDE Connect and Syncthing; Syncthing's web interface opens the first time to pair the phone.

items.name: Night Mode
items.blurb: Warmer screen colour for the evening, switched on and off from The Collar. Uses gammastep to set the monitor's colour temperature.

items.name: Game Player
items.blurb: Play NES, Super NES, Sega, Game Boy, Game Boy Advance, PlayStation and Nintendo 64 cartridges and discs in ZacOS 9: double-click a game file in the Sniffer and it runs in a Platinum-framed window, with a Game Player module in The Collar to quit it. The engines are RetroArch, mednafen and mupen64plus; PlayStation needs a Sony BIOS and Nintendo 64 needs firmware, which you supply.
